subject.title: chatCompletions: ignore request model when x-openclaw-agent-id header is present

question: Should a valid `x-openclaw-agent-id` make OpenAI-compatible requests ignore or tolerate a generic body `model`, despite the current documented agent-first model contract?
rationale: The code change is narrow, but it changes a public Gateway API contract and needs a parity decision across Chat Completions, Responses, and embeddings before an automated fix can safely choose behavior.

options.title: Adopt Header Precedence
options.body: Treat a generic body `model` as client compatibility metadata whenever a valid agent header selects the agent, and update shared resolver behavior plus docs/tests for selected endpoints.

options.title: Preserve Agent-First Contract
options.body: Continue requiring the body `model` to be `openclaw`, `openclaw/default`, or `openclaw/<agentId>`, and document SDK integrations around those values plus optional `x-openclaw-model`.

options.title: Decide Shared Endpoint Semantics First
options.body: Keep this open until Gateway owners choose one consistent precedence rule for Chat Completions, Responses, and embeddings.

options.title: Keep current contract
options.body: Require clients to send `openclaw`, `openclaw/default`, or `openclaw/<agentId>` in the body even when `x-openclaw-agent-id` is present, and clarify the SDK workaround in docs.

options.title: Add an explicit compatibility mode
options.body: Introduce a documented opt-in mode or header for SDK compatibility, accepting the added API surface to avoid changing default precedence.

recommendation.title: Decide Shared Endpoint Semantics First
recommendation.body: Keep this open until Gateway owners choose one consistent precedence rule for Chat Completions, Responses, and embeddings.

likelyOwner.reason: The requested change modifies the agent-first model contract that vincentkoc introduced and extended across the OpenAI-compatible Gateway surface.
